Backend 10/10 PASSED (test_iter35_payroll_auto.py): auto fields present, advances_hours/penalties_zl removed from record, payout formula correct, multi-advance summation, PUT with/without legacy fields tolerated, PDFs generated. Frontend verified live: TH headers 'Zaliczki' (no '(h)'), 'Kary' (no 'zl'); payroll-adv-auto-{eid} and payroll-pen-auto-{eid} are SPAN (read-only) for all 5 visible employees; input[type=number] has computed appearance:textfield (no spinners) and ::-webkit-inner-spin-button -webkit-appearance: textfield; .no-spinner CSS injected by skeletons.jsx. action_items: Older payroll tests (test_iter31_payroll.py, test_iter33_fixed_salary.py) reference removed legacy schema (advances_hours/penalties_zl in record) and old payout formula -> 5 tests fail by design. Recommend: rewrite those tests to match new schema or delete and mark iter35 as the canonical payroll test suite. Not blocking iter35 features.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payroll.py PayrollRecord still accepts legacy advances_hours/penalties_zl/housing_zl as Optional fields. They are persisted via update_one $set (raw.items() loop) into payroll_records collection, which clutters DB with deprecated columns. Consider stripping them from `raw` before persisting: raw.pop('advances_hours', None); raw.pop('penalties_zl', None); raw.pop('housing_zl', None).

routes/payroll.py list_payroll: For each request makes 4 sequential db round-trips (employees, hour_entries agg, sites, payroll_records) + 2 more for advances/penalties + 1 for lock. asyncio.gather of independent queries (employees+sites+advances+penalties+lock) would cut latency ~30-40%.

routes/payroll.py: defaults_cache pulled by $in on missing_emp_ids - if 200+ employees this lookup is fine, but sort([year,month]) on a large payroll_records collection without compound index (employee_id, year, month) could become slow.

skeletons.jsx side-effect CSS injection runs on import; if PayrollAdmin is lazy-loaded and CSS rule needed BEFORE PayrollAdmin renders (e.g., other input[number] elsewhere), spinners may still appear. Consider moving .no-spinner CSS to a global stylesheet (index.css) for guaranteed availability.
PayrollAdmin.js still has many client-side optimistic update branches; refactor into a small reducer for payout recomputation - 3+ duplicate formulas spotted across saveRecord/onChange handlers.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 5 visual checks: headers, span elements, count=5, appearance=textfield, CSS injection)

seed_data_creation: Test employee TEST_iter35 created in year=2027 month=9 with rate=30, bonus=100, 2 advances (250+100=350), 1 penalty (50). Cleanup via module-scoped fixture (delete advances/penalties/employee).
